note: Shared parity fixture. `core_cases`, `strata_cases`, `confidence_cases`, `outcome_cases` and `record_cases` are generated from the deployed platform grader (lambdas/calibration_core.py) and must be reproduced EXACTLY — not within a tolerance — by the extracted Python package and the JS port. `adapter_cases` cover the paste-a-ledger input layer that only the package and the JS port have; those are generated from the package and are two-way Python <-> JS. Regenerate with scripts/gen_calibration_vectors.py.

core_cases.description: nothing resolved — every number is None, never a fabricated zero
one confirmed call: n<3 so the label stays nascent
both outcomes identical — skill is undefined, not zero
stated 1.0/0.0 and always right — Brier 0, skill 1
the worst case — maximal confidence, always wrong
high stated confidence, mediocre reality — the classic LLM-coach failure
hedged low and kept being right — under-confident, still skilled
reliability without skill — must read not_yet_skillful, never well-calibrated
n>=12 and Brier<=0.15 — the only path to the top label
p==0.0 and p==1.0 must land in the first/last bin, not off the end
out-of-range / non-binary / unparseable entries are dropped, never coerced
n_bins is a parameter — the same pairs must re-bin identically everywhere
means that land on a rounding tie — the half-to-even trap the JS port has to reproduce

#3644: this Brier-skill sum lands on an exact 4-dp tie (-3.08625) where naive left-to-right float summation and math.fsum's correctly-rounded sum disagree by one ulp and round in OPPOSITE directions — a positive control pinned ON the tie, not moved off it. Both implementations must sum with the SAME rule (math.fsum / neumaierSum) to agree here.

strata_cases.description: coaches at 0.5/22% + interval forecasts at 0.8/79% — pooled skill against a pooled base rate manufactures +0.17; stratified reads negative, and the worst stratum's gap trips over-confident
a genuinely skilled stratum beside an unskilled one — pooled skill may be positive only because a stratum earned it
one stratum: the stratified reference IS the pooled reference, so skill equals score_pairs
an empty stratum and an all-identical-outcome stratum contribute no reference — skill undefined, not zero
no stratum reaches n>=5, so the pooled n-weighted gap drives the verdict

the worst-|gap| stratum is under-confident while the pool is not — [0.25, 1] in slot 5 lands the stratum's own skill on the #3644 4-dp tie (-3.08625), pinned here as a positive control now that both implementations share one summation rule
